{{Short description|Italian theoretical physicist}}

[[File:PietroGFre26_10_23.jpg|thumb|Pietro G. Frè (2023)]]

'''Pietro G. Frè''' (born 1952) is an [[Italians|Italian]] [[theoretical physicist]] and an [[emeritus]] full professor of the [[University of Turin]].

== Early life and education ==
Pietro G. Frè was born in [[Alessandria]], Italy in 1952.

== Career ==
Frè was a fellow at the Theoretical Division of CERN,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=D'Auria |first1=R |last2=Fre |first2=P |year=1985 |title=Universal Bose-Fermi mass-relations in Kaluza-Klein supergravity and harmonic analysis on coset manifolds with Killing spinors |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/0003491685901666 |journal=Annals of Physics |language=en |volume=162 |issue=2 |pages=372–412 |doi=10.1016/0003-4916(85)90166-6|url-access=subscription }}</ref> a post-doctoral fellow at the [[California Institute of Technology]] and [[Bielefeld University]] in the early years of his career. He was an [[associate professor]] at the [[University of Turin]], a full professor at the [[International School for Advanced Studies]] for six years, and, since 1996, a full professor at the [[University of Turin]] as the chair of [[general relativity]].

From 2009 to 2017 he was the scientific counselor of the Italian Embassy in Moscow. From 1996 to 2000 he was president of [[SIGRAV]] (Italian Society of General Relativity and Physics of Gravitation), and from 2017 to 2021 he was director of the [[Arnold Regge Center of Theoretical Physics]].

== Contributions ==
Among his major contributions in [[theoretical physics]], of particular note are the introduction of the [[nlab:D'Auria-Fre+formulation+of+supergravity|rheonomic formulation]] of [[supergravity]] (with R. D'Auria),<ref>{{Cite book |last=Frè |first=Pietro Giuseppe |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/978-94-007-5443-0 |title=Gravity, a Geometrical Course |date=2013 |publisher=Springer Netherlands |isbn=978-94-007-5442-3 |location=Dordrecht |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-94-007-5443-0}}</ref> the independent invention under the name of "Cartan Integrable Systems" of Free Differential Algebras<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Fre |first=P |date=1984-11-11 |title=Comments on the 6-index photon in d=11 supergravity and the gauging of free differential algebras |url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/0264-9381/1/6/005 |journal=Classical and Quantum Gravity |volume=1 |issue=6 |pages=L81–L90 |doi=10.1088/0264-9381/1/6/005 |bibcode=1984CQGra...1L..81F |s2cid=250814755 |issn=0264-9381}}</ref> and their extension with fermionic p-forms, the D'Auria-Frè algebra,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=D'Auria |first1=R. |last2=Fré |first2=P. |date=June 1982 |title=Geometric supergravity in D=11 and its hidden supergroup |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/0550321382903765 |journal=Nuclear Physics B |language=en |volume=201 |issue=1 |pages=101–140 |doi=10.1016/0550-3213(82)90376-5|bibcode=1982NuPhB.201..101D |url-access=subscription }}</ref> later evolved into the [[L-infinity algebra]]s, the geometric formulation of the [[eleven-dimensional supergravity]] (low-energy limit of [[M-theory]]), the geometric systematization of the N=2 Supergravity lagrangian<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Andrianopoli |first1=L. |last2=Bertolini |first2=M. |last3=Ceresole |first3=A. |last4=D'Auria |first4=R. |last5=Ferrara |first5=S. |last6=Fré |first6=P. |last7=Magri |first7=T. |date=September 1997 |title=N = 2 supergravity In recent years Pietro Frè has made original research in the context of [[Peter B. Kronheimer|Kronheimer construction]] and [[John McKay (mathematician)|McKay]] quivers.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Bruzzo |first1=Ugo |last2=Fino |first2=Anna |last3=Fré |first3=Pietro |date=January 2019 |title=The Kähler Quotient Resolution of $${{\mathbb{C}}^3/ \Gamma}$$ C 3 / Γ Singularities, the McKay Correspondence and $${D = 3\,\,\mathcal{N} = 2}$$ D = 3 N = 2 Chern–Simons Gauge Theories |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/s00220-018-3203-z |journal=Communications in Mathematical Physics |language=en |volume=365 |issue=1 |pages=93–214 |doi=10.1007/s00220-018-3203-z |arxiv=1710.01046 |s2cid=253744624 |issn=0010-3616}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Bruzzo |first1=Ugo |last2=Fino |first2=Anna |last3=Fré |first3=Pietro |last4=Grassi |first4=Pietro Antonio |last5=Markushevich |first5=Dimitri |date=November 2019 |title=Crepant resolutions of {{not a typo|ℂ}} 3 / Z 4 and the generalized Kronheimer construction (in view of the gauge/gravity correspondence) |journal=Journal of Geometry and Physics |language=en |volume=145 |page=103467 |doi=10.1016/j.geomphys.2019.06.018|s2cid=119281746 |doi-access=free |arxiv=1902.01060 }}</ref>

== Essays and Literature ==
Pietro Frè is also an essay and novel writer. He has published a few novels in Italian<ref>{{Cite book |last=Frè |first=Pietro |title=Il Concorso |publisher=Simonelli editore |year=2006 |isbn=978-88-7647-182-7 |language=Italian}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Frè |first=Pietro |title=Il Codice Cromlon |publisher=Simonelli Editore |year=2007 |isbn=978-88-7647-257-2 |language=Italian}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Frè |first=Pietro |title=Squame di Pesce |publisher=ZonaFranca Editore, Lucca |year=2018 |isbn=978-88-97025-17-7 |language=Italian}}</ref> and essays on the history of mathematical conceptions<ref>{{Cite book |last=Fré |first=Pietro Giuseppe |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/978-3-319-98023-2 |title=A Conceptual History of Space and Symmetry: From Plato to the Superworld |date=2018 |publisher=Springer International Publishing |isbn=978-3-319-98022-5 |location=Cham |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-3-319-98023-2|bibcode=2018chss.book.....F }}</ref> and an essay on the history of Ukraine and Russia.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Frè |first=Pietro |title=Kiev e Mosca nella Storia, amarezza e ricordi di un diplomatico pro tempore |publisher=Rubbettino Editore |year=2023 |isbn=978-88-498-7806-6 |language=Italian}}</ref>
